nodes.name: Schedule
nodes.notes:
What: Cron trigger that starts one content batch run every week.
In: Fires on cron 0 9 * * 0, so 09:00 every Sunday in the workflow timezone Africa/Cairo.
Out: One empty item that begins the run.

nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes:
What: HTTP entry point so a batch can be started by hand without waiting for Sunday.
In: A POST to the path instabay-studio, responseMode onReceived so the caller gets an instant reply.
Out: One item holding the request headers and body.

nodes.name: Init Run
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that stamps the run with an id, a start time, and which trigger fired it.
In: Either the empty schedule item or the webhook request item.
Out: One item with run_id wf2-<execution id>, started_at, trigger, and note taken from body.note.
Why: It tells webhook from schedule by looking for webhookUrl or headers on the incoming item.

nodes.name: Cost Before
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the OpenRouter account spend before any model runs.
In: The run item from Init Run; executeOnce so it calls only one time.
Out: The key info object; the brief later reads data.usage as the spend so far.
Why: GET on openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/key, set to continue on error so billing never kills the run.

nodes.name: Read Brand
nodes.notes:
What: Reads every row of the Brand tab so the run has the brand constitution.
In: The item from Cost Before; executeOnce so it reads only one time.
Out: All Brand rows, one item per row, carrying brand_name, posting_cadence and the hashtag lists.
Why: read operation on tab Brand of spreadsheet YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_ID.

nodes.name: Read Config
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the Config tab, the key and value settings that steer the run.
In: The items from Read Brand; executeOnce so it reads only one time.
Out: All Config rows, each with key, value and row_number.
Why: read on tab Config of the same spreadsheet; it holds batch_counter, posts_per_batch, approver_email.

nodes.name: Read Learnings
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the Learnings tab, the directives distilled from past batch performance.
In: The items from Read Config; executeOnce so it reads only one time.
Out: All Learnings rows with insight_type, dimension, directive, evidence and applied_in_batch.
Why: read on tab Learnings of the same spreadsheet; retryOnFail with maxTries 2, so one retry.

nodes.name: Read Calendar
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the Calendar tab so the run knows which topics were already posted.
In: The items from Read Learnings; executeOnce so it reads only one time.
Out: All Calendar rows, one item per past post row.
Why: read on tab Calendar of the same spreadsheet; the brief keeps rows with a post_id and takes topic.

nodes.name: Build Creative Brief
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that folds brand, config, learnings and past topics into one creative brief item.
In: Rows from the four sheet reads plus Init Run and Cost Before, all pulled by node name.
Out: One item with brand, config, batch_id, batch learnings, past topics, slots, formats and the post dates.
Why: It throws when the Brand tab is empty, and dates the batch one post per day from tomorrow.

nodes.name: Creative Director
nodes.notes:
What: Agent that writes the whole batch of Instagram posts for the Insta Bay resort, in Arabic and English.
In: The creative brief item; brand, learnings, used topics, dates, slots and formats go into the prompt.
Out: One item whose output holds a posts array with captions, hashtags, image prompt and reel fields.
Why: Its system prompt bans invented prices or facilities and requires native Arabic, never a translation.

options.systemMessage:
You are the Creative Director for Insta Bay, a Red Sea beach resort & spa in Hurghada, Egypt. The BRAND CONSTITUTION provided in the user message is law - never violate it.

Produce exactly the requested number of Instagram posts matching the required format mix EXACTLY (e.g. 1 reel, 1 carousel, 5 single images).

For EVERY post produce:
- post_id: 'b{batch}-p{n}' where batch is the batch number and n is 1..N in date order (e.g. 'b1-p3').
- date: the assigned date (one per provided date, in order).
- slot_time and slot_label: choose from the AVAILABLE TIME SLOTS. Deliberately VARY slots across the week - slot performance is being tested. If a learning directive names a slot, obey it for most posts while keeping at least one post in a different slot for comparison.
- format: 'reel' | 'carousel' | 'image'.
- pillar: a pillar name from the constitution, EXACTLY as written there. Respect the pillar mix percentages across the batch; if a learning redirects the mix, obey it while staying on-brand.
- topic: short unique topic, not in the used-topics list.
- caption_ar: WRITE THIS FIRST, natively in Egyptian Arabic following brand_voice_ar - exactly as a native Egyptian social media manager would write for Instagram: polished colloquial, warm, GCC-friendly, natural English loanwords (spa, sunset, check-in) where Egyptians actually use them. NEVER translate the English caption; write it as its own piece. First line must hook. 2-4 short lines with line breaks. End with the CTA per the constitution rules (DM / link in bio - never prices).
- caption_en: an independent English caption following brand_voice_en (NOT a translation of the Arabic). Hook first line, sensory middle, CTA end. 80-300 characters preferred.
- hashtags: array combining ALL hashtags_always PLUS 4-6 tags from the matching pillar's pool ONLY (total 7-11 tags). Never use a banned hashtag.
- image_prompt: a photorealistic image-generation prompt matching visual_direction and color_palette (golden hour, turquoise water, candid distance shots). No text in image, no logos, no recognizable faces. For carousels, describe slide 1.
- cta: the exact call-to-action phrase used.
- rationale: one sentence - why this topic/format/pillar/slot; cite the learning directive that shaped it if any (e.g. 'applies directive: ...').

For the ONE reel post additionally produce:
- reel_hook: the first-2-seconds spoken/visual hook.
- reel_storyboard: 5-7 scenes as [{scene, shot, action, on_screen_text, seconds}] totaling 15-30 seconds.
- reel_audio: an audio STYLE suggestion (e.g. 'calm tropical house build-up') - never name a specific copyrighted track.
- reel_cover_text: 3-5 words for the cover.

HARD RULES (never break): never invent specific facilities, prices, discounts, awards, room categories, restaurant names, or menu items beyond what the constitution guarantees (beach, turquoise water, snorkeling, diving, spa, relaxed-luxury resort). No fabricated reviews or guest quotes. Culturally respectful for conservative and international guests. Arabic is written natively, never translated.

Output ONLY JSON: {"posts": [ ... ]}. No commentary.

nodes.name: Gen Model
nodes.notes:
What: OpenRouter chat model node running anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, temperature 0.8, max 16000 tokens.
In: Prompts from the nodes it is attached to.
Out: The raw model reply those nodes then parse.
Why: Wired as ai_languageModel to Creative Director, Reviser and the Batch Schema autoFix parser.

nodes.name: Batch Schema
nodes.notes:
What: Structured output parser holding the JSON schema for a batch of posts.
In: The raw model text from Creative Director or Reviser.
Out: A parsed posts array; post_id, date, format, pillar, topic, both captions and hashtags are required.
Why: Attached as ai_outputParser to Creative Director and Reviser; autoFix on, so bad JSON gets repaired.

nodes.name: Brand Judge
nodes.notes:
What: Second agent that scores every post against a brand rubric and says pass or fail.
In: The posts array from Guard Batch plus the brand constitution pulled from Build Creative Brief.
Out: One item with an evaluations array: three 1 to 5 scores, a pass boolean and revision notes per post.
Why: pass is true only when all three scores are 4 or more; it runs on Judge Model, not Gen Model.

options.systemMessage:
You are an independent, strict brand-quality judge for Instagram content. You are NOT the writer and you gain nothing from being kind; judge adversarially but fairly against the rubric. For EACH post, reason step by step about each criterion first, then commit to integer scores.

Rubric (integers 1-5):
- brand_consistency: does the post obey the brand constitution - voice adjectives, pillar fit (pillar name must exist in the constitution), hashtag compliance (all always-on tags present, only pool tags added, no banned tags), CTA rules (DM / link in bio, no prices), no invented facilities/prices/offers? 5 = indistinguishable from a brand-book example; 4 = on-brand with minor nits; 3 = generic but inoffensive; 2 = noticeable violations; 1 = off-brand or invents facts.
- arabic_naturalness: would a native Egyptian social media manager write this caption_ar for Instagram? Penalize translation calques of the English caption, stiff MSA/fusha register, unnatural word order, awkward loanword use. Reward idiomatic Egyptian colloquial warmth that remains comfortable for GCC readers. 5 = fully native and idiomatic; 3 = understandable but clearly shaped by English phrasing; 1 = reads like machine translation.
- platform_fit: first-line hook strength, caption length (ideally 80-300 chars EN, hard max 2200), CTA present, format suitability (reel storyboard is 15-30s with a strong first-2-seconds hook and cover text of 3-5 words; carousel slide-1 concept leads), hashtag count 7-11.
- pass: true ONLY if all three scores are >= 4.
- revision_notes: if pass is false, give concrete, actionable fixes - quote the exact phrase or element to change and state the direction of the fix. Empty string if pass is true.

Output ONLY JSON: {"evaluations": [{"post_id": "...", "brand_consistency": 4, "arabic_naturalness": 4, "platform_fit": 4, "pass": true, "revision_notes": ""}]}. One evaluation per post, same post_id values.

nodes.name: Judge Model
nodes.notes:
What: OpenRouter chat model node running openai/gpt-4o-mini, temperature 0, max 8000 tokens.
In: Prompts from the nodes it is attached to.
Out: The raw scoring text those nodes then parse.
Why: Feeds Brand Judge, Re-Judge and Scores Schema as ai_languageModel; temperature 0 keeps scoring stable.

nodes.name: Scores Schema
nodes.notes:
What: Structured output parser holding the JSON schema for the judge scores.
In: The raw model text from Brand Judge or Re-Judge.
Out: A parsed evaluations array; post_id, the three scores and pass are required, revision_notes is not.
Why: Attached as ai_outputParser to Brand Judge and Re-Judge; autoFix on, so a bad score list is repaired.

nodes.name: Apply Verdicts And Lint
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that joins judge scores onto the posts and runs its own hard checks on each one.
In: Evaluations from Brand Judge on the input, posts from Creative Director, brand from Build Creative Brief.
Out: One item: posts with scores, lint_issues and needs_revision, plus any_revision, batch_issues, pre_scores.
Why: Lint checks tag count 7 to 11, always and banned tags, caption length, reel storyboard and one reel.

nodes.name: Needs Revision?
nodes.notes:
What: IF node that splits the batch into the fix path or the straight to publish path.
In: The single item from Apply Verdicts And Lint, testing the boolean any_revision.
Out: True output goes to Prep Revision; false output goes straight to Finalize Batch.

nodes.name: Prep Revision
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that gathers the posts, the open issues and any human feedback for the revision agent.
In: From Needs Revision? true or Approval? Changes; posts from Merge Final Batch or Apply Verdicts And Lint.
Out: One item with posts, batch_issues, human_feedback, brand and batch_id.
Why: The Merge-first fallback lets one node serve the auto fix pass and the human change-request loop.

nodes.name: Reviser
nodes.notes:
What: Agent that rewrites only the failing posts and applies human feedback to the whole batch.
In: The prep item with posts, judge notes, lint issues, batch issues, human feedback and the brand.
Out: One item whose output holds the full posts array, with passing posts returned unchanged.
Why: Its prompt says human feedback outranks the judge notes whenever the two conflict.

options.systemMessage:
You are the Revision Editor for Insta Bay Instagram content. Apply the judge's revision_notes and fix every listed lint_issue for each post that has needs_revision=true, and apply the HUMAN FEEDBACK to the whole batch when present (human feedback outranks judge notes on any conflict). Fix batch-level issues too (e.g. wrong reel count - convert the most cinematic post to the required format).

Rules:
- Posts that passed and are untouched by human feedback: return them VERBATIM, unchanged.
- Keep post_id, date, slot_time, slot_label, format, pillar stable unless a note or the human feedback explicitly requires changing them.
- caption_ar stays natively-written Egyptian Arabic (never a translation); improving it means making it MORE idiomatic, not more formal.
- All brand hard rules still apply: no invented facilities/prices/offers/reviews; hashtags = all always-on + pool tags only, 7-11 total, no banned tags.
- Return every post with ALL its fields (including reel fields for the reel).

Output ONLY JSON: {"posts": [ ... ]} in exactly the same schema as the input posts.

nodes.name: Re-Judge
nodes.notes:
What: Agent that scores the revised batch again using the same rubric as the first judge.
In: The revised posts array from Reviser plus the brand from Build Creative Brief.
Out: One item with a fresh evaluations array, exactly the same shape as the first judge.
Why: Its system message is identical to Brand Judge, so before and after scores stay comparable.

options.systemMessage:
You are an independent, strict brand-quality judge for Instagram content. You are NOT the writer and you gain nothing from being kind; judge adversarially but fairly against the rubric. For EACH post, reason step by step about each criterion first, then commit to integer scores.

Rubric (integers 1-5):
- brand_consistency: does the post obey the brand constitution - voice adjectives, pillar fit (pillar name must exist in the constitution), hashtag compliance (all always-on tags present, only pool tags added, no banned tags), CTA rules (DM / link in bio, no prices), no invented facilities/prices/offers? 5 = indistinguishable from a brand-book example; 4 = on-brand with minor nits; 3 = generic but inoffensive; 2 = noticeable violations; 1 = off-brand or invents facts.
- arabic_naturalness: would a native Egyptian social media manager write this caption_ar for Instagram? Penalize translation calques of the English caption, stiff MSA/fusha register, unnatural word order, awkward loanword use. Reward idiomatic Egyptian colloquial warmth that remains comfortable for GCC readers. 5 = fully native and idiomatic; 3 = understandable but clearly shaped by English phrasing; 1 = reads like machine translation.
- platform_fit: first-line hook strength, caption length (ideally 80-300 chars EN, hard max 2200), CTA present, format suitability (reel storyboard is 15-30s with a strong first-2-seconds hook and cover text of 3-5 words; carousel slide-1 concept leads), hashtag count 7-11.
- pass: true ONLY if all three scores are >= 4.
- revision_notes: if pass is false, give concrete, actionable fixes - quote the exact phrase or element to change and state the direction of the fix. Empty string if pass is true.

Output ONLY JSON: {"evaluations": [{"post_id": "...", "brand_consistency": 4, "arabic_naturalness": 4, "platform_fit": 4, "pass": true, "revision_notes": ""}]}. One evaluation per post, same post_id values.

nodes.name: Merge Final Batch
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that merges revised posts over the originals and re-runs the hashtag lint.
In: Revised posts from Reviser, base posts from Prep Revision, new evaluations from Re-Judge on the input.
Out: One item with revised true and merged posts carrying new scores, _pre scores and revision_count + 1.
Why: It keeps the first pass brand and arabic scores as _pre fields, taken from Apply Verdicts And Lint.

nodes.name: Finalize Batch
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that turns each post into one flat sheet row with a publish time and an image URL.
In: One item of posts, from the false branch of Needs Revision? or from Merge Final Batch.
Out: One row per post: publish_at in Cairo time, space-joined hashtags, image_url, status pending, scores.
Why: image_url calls image.pollinations.ai at 1080x1350 with an FNV hash of post_id as the fixed seed.

nodes.name: Upsert Calendar
nodes.notes:
What: Writes every finished post row into the Calendar tab, inserting new ones and updating old ones.
In: One item per post from Finalize Batch.
Out: The written rows, passed on to the approval email step.
Why: appendOrUpdate on tab Calendar matching on post_id, so re-running a batch never duplicates rows.

nodes.name: Format Approval Email
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that builds the HTML review sheet showing every post in the batch.
In: All the post rows written by Upsert Calendar.
Out: One item with subject, html, batch_id, posts_count and approval_url.
Why: It reads $execution.resumeFormUrl, the Approval Gate link, before that Wait node has run.

nodes.name: Approval?
nodes.notes:
What: Switch that routes the human decision to the approve path or back into the revision loop.
In: The form answer item from Approval Gate, reading the Decision field.
Out: Output Approve goes to Mark Approved; output Changes goes back to Prep Revision.
Why: Approve all and Request changes are the only two dropdown options, so every submission matches.

nodes.name: Mark Approved
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that builds a small update row per post marking it approved right now.
In: All the rows written earlier by Upsert Calendar, pulled by node name.
Out: One item per post with only post_id, status approved and an approved_at timestamp.
Why: It rebuilds from Upsert Calendar because the form answer item carries no post data.

nodes.name: Update Approved
nodes.notes:
What: Writes the approved status back onto each post row in the Calendar tab.
In: One slim item per post from Mark Approved.
Out: The updated Calendar rows.
Why: appendOrUpdate on tab Calendar matching on post_id, so only status and approved_at change.

nodes.name: Cost After
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the OpenRouter account spend again once the batch has been approved.
In: The updated rows from Update Approved; executeOnce so it calls only one time.
Out: The key info object; Run Stats reads data.usage as the spend after the run.
Why: GET on openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/key, continue on error so billing never blocks the run.

nodes.name: Run Stats
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that computes run duration, model cost and cost per post.
In: started_at and cost_before from the brief, spend from Cost After, post count from Mark Approved.
Out: One RunLog row with run_id, workflow WF2-content-studio, batch_id, timings, cost and posts_count.
Why: Cost is the difference between the two OpenRouter spend reads, rounded to four decimals.

nodes.name: Log Run
nodes.notes:
What: Appends the run statistics row to the RunLog tab.
In: The single stats row from Run Stats.
Out: The appended row, passed on to the counter bump.
Why: append operation on tab RunLog of the same spreadsheet; retryOnFail with maxTries 2, so one retry.

nodes.name: Bump Batch Counter
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that reads the current batch_counter from Config and produces its next value.
In: All Config rows pulled from Read Config, searched for the key batch_counter.
Out: One item with row_number, key batch_counter and the value raised by one.
Why: It throws when the batch_counter row is missing, so the counter can never silently stop moving.

nodes.name: Write Batch Counter
nodes.notes:
What: Writes the new batch number back into the Config tab.
In: The single row from Bump Batch Counter.
Out: The updated Config row; this is the last node of the run.
Why: update operation on tab Config matching on row_number, not on key, so it edits that exact row.

nodes.name: Guard Batch
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that throws when the generated batch is missing posts, the wrong size, or has bad ids.
In: The parsed output object from Creative Director.
Out: One item carrying the same output object, so Brand Judge still reads output.posts.
Why: It stops truncated generations and autofix hallucinations before they reach the judge or the sheet.

nodes.name: Approval Link Row
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that builds one RunLog shaped row carrying the approval form link.
In: The email item from Format Approval Email plus run_id, batch_id and started_at from the brief.
Out: One row with workflow WF2-approval-link and the approval URL sitting in the notes column.
Why: The link is saved to the sheet before the email sends, so a failed send still leaves it recoverable.

nodes.name: Log Approval Link
nodes.notes:
What: Appends the approval link row to the RunLog tab.
In: The single row from Approval Link Row.
Out: The appended row, passed on to the email step.
Why: append operation on tab RunLog of the same spreadsheet; retryOnFail with maxTries 2, so one retry.

nodes.name: Notify Approval
nodes.notes:
What: Sends the HTML approval email to the approver through Gmail.
In: Recipient from config.approver_email, subject and html from Format Approval Email.
Out: The Gmail send result, passed to the Approval Gate.
Why: Set to continue on error, so a Gmail failure still lets the run reach the waiting form.

nodes.name: Approval Gate
nodes.notes:
What: Wait node that pauses the run and shows a web form with the batch and a decision.
In: Reached from Notify Approval; the run then waits until a human submits the form.
Out: One item with the Decision choice and the Feedback textarea text.
Why: The form holds the rendered batch HTML, a required Decision dropdown and a free text feedback box.

parameters.formDescription: Review the batch below, pick a decision, and submit. 'Request changes' + feedback sends the batch back to the Reviser.
